title: Hutchinson & Bulkeley v. Western Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC held that Presbytery did not err through its Commission’s treatment of RE Neill Payne’s views, including those expressed in his November 26, 2007 “Africa e-mail”; the sole specification was not sustained.
first_summary: Hutchinson and Bulkeley challenged Presbytery’s refusal to condemn RE Neill Payne’s views in a circulated “Africa e-mail.” The SJC did not sustain the complaint because the brief e-mail and linked article did not present Payne’s views fully enough for responsible adjudication, and courts may not condemn a church officer’s allegedly erroneous opinions without due process. The SJC deferred to Presbytery’s evaluation.
summary: Hutchinson and Bulkeley challenged Presbytery’s refusal to condemn RE Neill Payne’s views in a circulated “Africa e-mail.” The SJC did not sustain the complaint. It held that a presbytery may not condemn a church officer’s allegedly erroneous opinions without due process and that four sentences, an approving newspaper reference, and the Commission’s summary did not present Payne’s views fully enough for responsible adjudication. The SJC rejected race or intelligence as the primary determinant of a nation’s fate, while allowing the e-mail to be used as evidence in formal charges.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The case heading and judgment identify Case 2008-18 as Hutchinson and Bulkeley’s complaint against WCP; the full SJC amended the panel draft (lines 536–544, 594; printed p. 178).
evidence_notes.dispute: Complainants alleged that Presbytery’s Commission should have condemned Payne’s views expressed in the November 26, 2007 e-mail (lines 544–556; printed p. 178).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The specification was not sustained because condemnation required due process and the abbreviated material was insufficient for adjudicating Payne’s views; the SJC deferred to Presbytery (lines 544–564; printed pp. 178–179).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC disclaimed the suggested race-and-intelligence premise and permitted the e-mail’s later use as evidence in formal charges (lines 558–570; printed p. 179).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference in Case 2008-18.
